abstract.text:
We analyze the most general case of third-order Chern–Simons-like theories of massive 3D gravity.
Results show the conditions for finding the unitary regions on the parameter space. There exists
(n − 1)th order theories on the boundary of a unitary nth order model on parameter space under
certain conditions, as the first example recently demonstrated from the bimetric generalization of
exotic massive gravity. We investigated the mechanism that causes this type of transition for thirdorder models. Hamiltonian analysis of the theory also presents that ghost and no-ghost regions can
be separated by Chern–Simons theories.

On the other hand, GR in three dimensions (3D) yields
a trivial theory without any local degree of freedom [1].

However, a degree of freedom is attainable by adding a
gravitational Chern–Simons term to an Einstein–Hilbert
action in 3D, which is called topological massive gravity
(TMG) [2].

Another example, new massive gravity (NMG) [3], is a paritypreserving fourth-order model and its linearization gives
the Fierz–Pauli theory [4] with two massive graviton
modes with helicity ±2.

If one abandons the paritypreserving condition on NMG the theory can be extended
to general massive gravity (GMG) [5] that has ±2 helicity states with different masses and gives both TMG and
NMG as a limit.

Other than NMG and GMG, there is
another fourth-order theory called exotic massive gravity
[6], which is a parity-odd theory with an intriguing feature called third-way consistency [7].

In the 3D case, the first-order formulation
of the bimetric theory is known as zwei-dreibein gravity
(ZDG) [8] that has a limiting case to NMG.

sections.summary: Studies the eight-dimensional parameter space, shows that det(g)=0 signals lower-flavor degeneration, and works through an example flow where a 3→2 transition occurs and the resulting equations reduce to Einstein–Cartan theory. It concludes that the general third-order CS-like theory has unitary and nonunitary regions separated by hypersurfaces, with lower-order theories appearing at the boundaries and Chern–Simons theories separating ghost and no-ghost regions.
